## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | The journal's own pages disagree, both read in a real browser on 2026-11-24. (1) The about-this-journal page says all research articles undergo 'rigorous double-anonymised peer review', based on initial editor screening and refereeing by at least two anonymous external referees; 'Collective Writing' articles undergo editor screening only and editors invite open responses published as part of the article (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rept20/about-this-journal). (2) The instructions-for-authors page says that after the editor's suitability check the paper is 'single anonymous peer reviewed by two independent, anonymous expert[s]' (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20). The older Wayback instructions (2022-10-23) also said single anonymous. Which is operative cannot be settled from the pages; check with the editorial office before submitting. The instructions add that a manuscript already on a preprint server cannot be guaranteed anonymity |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. No source read |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Not as standard practice per anything read. The journal ran an open peer review experiment for some collectively written articles from 2016, described in an editorial (https://doi.org/10.1080/00131857.2020.1846519; Crossref confirms the item, vol. 55 issue 2, pp. 133-140, https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1080/00131857.2020.1846519; the editorial text itself was not read). Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | Blank. No source found |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No source found |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Partly. The journal's instructions page (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24) has a 'Declaration of generative AI use' item in its checklist: a statement is required saying whether and how generative AI was used, and, if not used, saying so (suggested wording given); it refers to the publisher's AI guidance for permitted scenarios. The permitted-use rules themselves are the Taylor & Francis publisher-wide policy |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with a mandatory disclosure statement |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory disclosure; same rubric as the Mind entry) |
| **Summary** | Publisher policy: AI tools cannot be listed as authors. Authors must acknowledge any generative AI use, naming the tool and version, how it was used and why, in a dedicated disclosure statement. AI-generated text or code without rigorous revision, and AI creation or manipulation of research images, are prohibited. AI may assist translation and copyediting with a declaration. Reviewers and editors may not upload unpublished manuscripts into AI tools. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20 (journal declaration item); https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/ and https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/editorial-policies/defining-authorship-research-paper/ (publisher policy) |

## Format

> Source for the general rules: the journal's instructions for authors, https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24. Values that differ from the 2022-10-23 Wayback copy are marked. The 2019 society call and the current special-issue call are listed separately because they set their own lengths. A malformed duplicate table fragment that sat below this table in the earlier version was removed.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Live instructions: the journal 'accepts the following types of article: original articles'; English only (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24). The journal's own 2019 special-issue call lists short commentaries, research notes and full papers (https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf). OpenAlex type counts for 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23: 559 articles, 64 book reviews, 60 editorials (retrieved 2026-11-23); the instructions do not list book reviews or editorials, and the board lists a reviews editor, so these appear to be commissioned or editorial routes (inference) |
| **Word limit** | 'A typical paper for this journal should be no more than 6000 words', inclusive of tables, references, footnotes and endnotes; authors are asked to include a word count (live instructions, https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; unchanged from the 2022-10-23 copy). Special-issue lengths: 600 words for short commentaries, 1000 for research notes, 6000 for full papers in the 2019 call (https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf); about 6,000 words for the 'Intelligence Beyond the Artificial' call (https://callforpapers.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/intelligence-beyond-the-artificial/, retrieved 2026-11-23). Crossref page ranges give a median article length of 12 pages over 871 of 877 records with parseable ranges, 2021-2026 (includes book reviews and editorials) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Blank. The instructions word the limit as a typical-paper ceiling; no statement on exceptions found |
| **Abstract limit** | Unstructured abstract of 200 words; between 3 and 4 keywords; optional graphical abstract of at most 525 pixels width (live instructions, https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; same as the 2022 copy) |
| **Reference limit** | No separate cap found; references count inside the 6000 words (live instructions, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24). The reference style is linked ('this reference style') without being named in the page text, plus an EndNote style |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplemental material (video, filesets, audio) is published online via Figshare (live instructions, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables: supply editable files, and tables should present new information rather than duplicate the text; units: SI; figure resolution requirements are given (live instructions, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24). Colour is free online; print colour is charged |
| **Style / submission format** | Live instructions (read in a real browser on 2026-11-24): any spelling style if consistent; single quotation marks with long quotations indented; Word or LaTeX (LaTeX as PDF plus a zip of source files); figures saved separately; Routledge submission portal; Crossref screening for unoriginal material during review and production; all authors give full name and affiliation on the cover page, affiliation being where the research was conducted. The page also lists a generic empirical section order (introduction, materials and methods, results, discussion) as template text; Crossref title counts show 'empirical', 'interview' or 'survey' in only 18 of 877 titles (structure of articles was not sampled). Special-issue calls name APA referencing (https://callforpapers.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/intelligence-beyond-the-artificial/) |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** One scope condition is stated by the journal itself: 'manuscripts must be germane to the ongoing conversations and dialogues of educational philosophy', even when they come from other areas of educational research (live aims text, https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rept20/about-this-journal, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; the same wording is in the 2024-03-04 home-page copy https://web.archive.org/web/20240304155049/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rept20, the society's page https://pesa.org.au/our-publications/educational-philosophy-and-theory-epat, and the 2019 call https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf).
- **What kind of engagement?** Engagement with educational-philosophy debate, not a named theoretical school. The 2024-03-04 aims text lists curriculum theory, educational administration, politics of education, educational history, educational policy and higher education as areas of applied educational research the journal has published, and encourages submissions from collateral areas in education, the arts and sciences and from professional educators.
- **Article type and length**: original articles only in the live instructions, up to about 6000 words including references, an unstructured 200-word abstract and 3 to 4 keywords (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24; same as the 2022-10-23 copy). The 2019 special-issue call lists short commentaries (600 words), research notes (1000) and full papers (6000). The live about page also says 'Collective Writing' articles undergo editor screening and carry published open responses (https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rept20/about-this-journal).
- **Special-issue framing seen**: the current call "Intelligence Beyond the Artificial" (guest editors affiliated with East China Normal University) asks what human capacities remain essential as AI spreads, invites essays and research-based analysis of about 6,000 words in APA style, with abstracts due 1 December 2026, notification by 31 December 2026 and full manuscripts due 1 May 2027 (https://callforpapers.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/intelligence-beyond-the-artificial/). Two earlier calls shown on the journal home copy of 2024-03-04: "South Korea as Method" and "Critical Times?" (see Epistemological section for the URL). A call on memory and autoethnographic inquiry in higher education: https://think.taylorandfrancis.com/special_issues/memory-meaning-and-autoethnographic-inquiry-as-epistemological-sources-sitting-with-the-crisis-of-higher-education/ (title and 6,000-word figure from a search summary; the page returned 404 on direct fetch).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what happens to out-of-scope submissions, and no desk-rejection data exists (SciRev 0 reviews: https://scirev.org/journal/educational-philosophy-and-theory/).

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are records of this source dated 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (OpenAlex: 696 records, all types, 550 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the term; shares below use 696 as the denominator (conservative, since a title match counts for records without abstracts). Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement, and none was found. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. A second, title-only check uses Crossref (877 records, 0% with abstract; counts are lower bounds). This rescoring replaces the earlier count-based scale (1-29 = 1, 30-99 = 2, 100+ = 3).

| Qualitative interviews | 2 | "interview" 28 (4.0%), "qualitative" 11, "semi-structured" 0, "thematic analysis" 0 (OpenAlex, 696 records). Crossref titles: "qualitative" 3, "empirical", "case study", "interview" or "survey" 18 of 877 |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | The live instructions require a written statement in the Methods for all original research papers involving humans, animals, plants, biological material, protected or non-public datasets, collections or sites, confirming ethical approval from the appropriate ethics committee or institutional review board and informed consent where relevant; where approval for non-interventional studies such as surveys is not required, authors must explain why; where no ethics committee exists they are advised to contact the Editor (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24). A consent statement is also required for participants in qualitative or quantitative research. The work is mostly non-empirical by keyword counts (OpenAlex, see Methodological Preferences), so the rule applies to a minority of papers |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author papers are common: 89 of the first 200 articles returned by OpenAlex for 2021-11-23 to 2026-11-23 (not a random sample; retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Affiliation rule (live instructions, https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24): all authors give full name and affiliation on the cover page, defined as where the research was conducted; no independent-scholar rule is stated. The 2023 board copy listed 11 of 137 named reviewers as independent scholars (older figure, https://web.archive.org/web/20230616124608/https://www.tandfonline.com/action/journalInformation?show=editorialBoard&journalCode=rept20). The 2019 call invites contributions from professional educators and from arts and sciences (https://pesa.org.au/images/docs/REPT_SI_CFP_template.pdf) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | None found: the live instructions (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24) contain no data-availability or data-sharing section (searched the page text for 'data availability' and 'data sharing': not present); supplemental material goes to Figshare |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Unclear, because the journal's two live pages disagree (double-anonymised on the about page, single anonymous on the instructions page; see Peer Review). Author names and affiliations go on the cover page; a manuscript on a preprint server loses any anonymity guarantee (live instructions, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24). Pre-submission preprints are allowed by the publisher (https://authorservices.taylorandfrancis.com/research-impact/sharing-versions-of-journal-articles/) |
| **AI use** | Disclosure statement required by the journal's instructions, including a statement when AI was not used (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24); AI cannot be an author (https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/) |
| **Open access and cost** | Hybrid (Open Select); the live instructions state no submission, publication or page charges for the non-OA route; the OA APC amount was not readable (interactive finder, see Open Access); 169 of 559 recent articles are hybrid OA in OpenAlex (https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24) |
| **Originality screening** | All submissions are screened for unoriginal material with Crossref similarity checking during peer review and production (live instructions, https://www.tandfonline.com/action/authorSubmission?show=instructions&journalCode=rept20, read in a real browser on 2026-11-24) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Scope**: the journal's own aims text states manuscripts must be germane to the ongoing conversations of educational philosophy (Framing Requirements; archived home page, https://web.archive.org/web/20240304155049/https://www.tandfonline.com/journals/rept20). A paper with no engagement with that conversation is outside the stated scope.
- **Length**: a typical paper should not exceed 6000 words, references and notes included (Format; archived instructions, 2022-10-23). A longer manuscript departs from the stated norm; whether exceptions are granted is not stated.
- **AI use**: undisclosed generative AI use, unrevised AI-generated text, or AI-manipulated research images breach the publisher policy (AI Policy, https://taylorandfrancis.com/our-policies/ai-policy/).
- No other hard blocker is supported by a fact I could read; ethics-approval and data-sharing rules are unknown (Practical Concerns blanks), and the archived instructions are from 2022.

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the publisher-reported first-decision figure of about 122-126 days (Review Cycle Time; unverified secondary summary) implies roughly four months before the first decision. Total time to acceptance is unknown.
- **Open access cost**: green deposit of the accepted manuscript is subject to a typical 18-month embargo for social-science and humanities journals on the publisher page (Preprint Policy; not confirmed for this journal); gold open access carries an APC whose amount was not found (Open Access).
- **Anonymisation**: the archived instructions describe single-anonymous review with names and affiliations on the cover page (Peer Review, Format, Practical Concerns), so that copy asks for no author-identity redaction; a preprint removes any anonymity guarantee. An earlier version of this entry said double-anonymised, from a search summary; that was corrected here, and the live page could not be read to confirm which is current.

### Best Suited For

- Conceptual and philosophical analysis of education: "philosophical" appears in 123 of 696 records and "theoretical" in 83 (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Work engaging Continental, critical, decolonial, Indigenous or Asian traditions, or philosophy of technology and AI in education: counts of 22-38 for decolonial and Indigenous, 20 for Confucian, 21 for artificial intelligence, and the most cited 2021-2025 article is on ChatGPT-4 (Epistemological & Political Leanings, Sensitive Topics).
- Sole-authored essays: 89 of 200 sampled articles are single-author (Voice & Style).
- Authors without a university affiliation: 11 of 137 named reviewers on the 2023 board page are listed as independent scholars (Reviewer Pool Characteristics); this says nothing about acceptance odds for such authors.

### Not Recommended For

- Primarily empirical or quantitative studies: "survey" 6, "quantitative" 3, "randomized" 0, "interview" 28 of 696 records (Methodological Preferences). The counts show these are rare here, not that they are rejected.
- Systematic reviews: "systematic review" appears in 0 of 696 records (Methodological Preferences); this shows the form is absent from titles and abstracts, not that it is rejected.
- Anyone needing a verified turnaround figure before choosing: the only figures (about 122-126 days to first decision) come from search summaries that were not verified (Review Cycle Time). The word limit is now known from the archived instructions (Format).

### Rejection Fallback Chain

> No source states where rejected authors usually go. The rows below are topical neighbours that already exist in this corpus, listed only because they share the subject area (philosophy of education); they are not a claim about acceptance odds.
